key_insight: A five-agent "Trust but Verify" audit layer can substantially reduce LLM recommendations of banned or withdrawn drugs in clinical question answering.
clinical_relevance: For safety-critical healthcare use, the framework helps shift model behavior from unsafe medication suggestions toward appropriate refusal and regulatory compliance.
method: Built a 5-agent post-hoc auditing system on top of a single LLM backbone
Created 103 adversarial multiple-choice clinical questions featuring historically correct but now banned substances
Compared GPT-OSS, Llama-3, and Falcon-3 under vanilla vs agentic settings using HER, label accuracy, pointwise score, and CF
evidence_signal: Across open-access models, the agentic setup reduced hallucination error rate by about 53% and moved pointwise scores from -0.25 toward 0.0.
watch_item: Performance was tested on a focused adversarial benchmark, so real-world deployment still needs continuous regulatory updates and validation across broader clinical contexts.
paper_title: Trust but Verify: Mitigating Medical Hallucinations via Post-Hoc Adversarial Auditing and Multi-Agent Feedback Loops
